children.text: An N by N lattice, \(N>1\), contains \(N^2\) identical uniform equilateral triangular plates of side l and mass M. Equal-length massless rods connect freely hinged vertices. Four tubes confine the N edge vertices to slide along rails. The tubes form a diamond with fixed 60 and 120 degree corners. The top tube is horizontal, with top-left vertex A(0,0) fixed. The lattice has one degree of freedom \(0\le\alpha\le60^\circ\). Triangles are indexed \((m,n)\), \(0\le m,n<N\), with vertices A,B,C in the diagrams. Motion lies in the xy plane, y positive upward, and potential zero at y=0. A plate has central inertia \(Ml^2/12\). Use gravitational acceleration g.

statement.text:
Mechanics of a Deformable Lattice
An N by N lattice, \(N>1\), contains \(N^2\) identical uniform equilateral triangular plates of side l and mass M. Equal-length massless rods connect freely hinged vertices. Four tubes confine the N edge vertices to slide along rails. The tubes form a diamond with fixed 60 and 120 degree corners. The top tube is horizontal, with top-left vertex A(0,0) fixed. The lattice has one degree of freedom \(0\le\alpha\le60^\circ\). Triangles are indexed \((m,n)\), \(0\le m,n<N\), with vertices A,B,C in the diagrams. Motion lies in the xy plane, y positive upward, and potential zero at y=0. A plate has central inertia \(Ml^2/12\). Use gravitational acceleration g.


A.1. Four-plate potential

For N=2, find total potential energy as a function of angle.
A.2. Four-plate equilibrium
Find the equilibrium angle for N=2.
A.3. Four-plate oscillation
Find kinetic energy in terms of \(\Delta\dot\alpha\) for small oscillations and the ordinary frequency.
B.1. General lattice equilibrium
Find the equilibrium angle for arbitrary N.
B.2. Large-lattice scaling
At equilibrium as \(N\to\infty\), find exponents in \(\Delta E_p\propto N^{\gamma_1}\), \(E_k\propto N^{\gamma_2}\), and \(f_{E}^{\prime}\propto N^{\gamma_3}\), for fixed small angle and angular-speed perturbations.
C.1. Optimal force point

Choose one of the \(3N^2\) vertices where a force can maintain \(\alpha=60^\circ\) with minimum magnitude.
C.2. Minimum holding force
Find this force magnitude and its direction \(\theta_F\) as shown in the diagram.

children.text: The first plate centre is at \(y_{00}=-l\sin(\pi/6+\alpha)/\sqrt3\); each row is lower by \(\sqrt3l\cos\alpha\). Thus \[E_p=4Mg\,y_{00}-2\sqrt3Mgl\cos\alpha=-\frac23Mgl(4\sqrt3\cos\alpha+3\sin\alpha).\]
Zero first derivative of the potential gives \(4\sqrt3\sin\alpha_E=3\cos\alpha_E\), so \(\alpha_E=\arctan(\sqrt3/4)=0.40864\,\mathrm{rad}\). The second derivative is positive.

Plate-centre coordinates are \[x_{mn}=(2m+n)l\cos\alpha+\frac l{\sqrt3}\cos(\alpha+\pi/6),\quad y_{mn}=-\sqrt3nl\cos\alpha-\frac l{\sqrt3}\sin(\alpha+\pi/6).\] Differentiate and sum \(M(\dot x^2+\dot y^2)/2\) over four plates. This gives \(164Ml^2(\Delta\dot\alpha)^2/57\). Plate spin adds \(Ml^2(\Delta\dot\alpha)^2/6\). Therefore \[E_k=\frac{347}{114}Ml^2(\Delta\dot\alpha)^2.\] Also \(\Delta E_p=\sqrt{57}Mgl(\Delta\alpha)^2/3\). Taking the ratio of the two quadratic coefficients yields \[f_E=\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{38\sqrt{57}}{347}\frac gl}.\]

The potential curvature grows as \(N^3\). Since \(\alpha_{E}^{\prime}\sim1/N\), differentiated centre coordinates remain order l per plate even at indices of order N. Each plate contributes order one translational and rotational inertia, so total inertia grows as \(N^2\). Hence \((\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3)=(3,2,1/2)\). The small-angle limit is taken locally about each equilibrium before comparing N scaling.
Virtual work requires \(F|\partial\mathbf r/\partial\alpha|\ge|\partial E_p/\partial\alpha|\). The largest vertex displacement per angle is at C(N-1,N-1), so choose that vertex.

At \(\alpha=\pi/3\), \(dE_p/d\alpha=3(N-1)N^2Mgl/4\). The C(N-1,N-1) derivative is \((3N-2)l(-\sqrt3/2,1/2)\). A force along that derivative supplies positive virtual work, giving \[F_{min}=\frac{3(N-1)N^2}{4(3N-2)}Mg,\qquad\theta_F=5\pi/6.\] The force is 150 degrees from positive x, rather than necessarily perpendicular to the line from the fixed vertex.

solution.text:
Mechanics of a Deformable Lattice
A.1. Four-plate potential
The first plate centre is at \(y_{00}=-l\sin(\pi/6+\alpha)/\sqrt3\); each row is lower by \(\sqrt3l\cos\alpha\). Thus \[E_p=4Mg\,y_{00}-2\sqrt3Mgl\cos\alpha=-\frac23Mgl(4\sqrt3\cos\alpha+3\sin\alpha).\]
A.2. Four-plate equilibrium
Zero first derivative of the potential gives \(4\sqrt3\sin\alpha_E=3\cos\alpha_E\), so \(\alpha_E=\arctan(\sqrt3/4)=0.40864\,\mathrm{rad}\). The second derivative is positive.
A.3. Four-plate oscillation
Plate-centre coordinates are \[x_{mn}=(2m+n)l\cos\alpha+\frac l{\sqrt3}\cos(\alpha+\pi/6),\quad y_{mn}=-\sqrt3nl\cos\alpha-\frac l{\sqrt3}\sin(\alpha+\pi/6).\] Differentiate and sum \(M(\dot x^2+\dot y^2)/2\) over four plates. This gives \(164Ml^2(\Delta\dot\alpha)^2/57\). Plate spin adds \(Ml^2(\Delta\dot\alpha)^2/6\). Therefore \[E_k=\frac{347}{114}Ml^2(\Delta\dot\alpha)^2.\] Also \(\Delta E_p=\sqrt{57}Mgl(\Delta\alpha)^2/3\). Taking the ratio of the two quadratic coefficients yields \[f_E=\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{38\sqrt{57}}{347}\frac gl}.\]
B.1. General lattice equilibrium
Summing plate heights gives \[E_p=-\frac{N^2Mgl}{6}\left[\sqrt3(3N-2)\cos\alpha+3\sin\alpha\right].\] Differentiate: \[\alpha_{E}^{\prime}=\arctan\frac{\sqrt3}{3N-2}.\]
B.2. Large-lattice scaling
The potential curvature grows as \(N^3\). Since \(\alpha_{E}^{\prime}\sim1/N\), differentiated centre coordinates remain order l per plate even at indices of order N. Each plate contributes order one translational and rotational inertia, so total inertia grows as \(N^2\). Hence \((\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3)=(3,2,1/2)\). The small-angle limit is taken locally about each equilibrium before comparing N scaling.
C.1. Optimal force point
Virtual work requires \(F|\partial\mathbf r/\partial\alpha|\ge|\partial E_p/\partial\alpha|\). The largest vertex displacement per angle is at C(N-1,N-1), so choose that vertex.
C.2. Minimum holding force
At \(\alpha=\pi/3\), \(dE_p/d\alpha=3(N-1)N^2Mgl/4\). The C(N-1,N-1) derivative is \((3N-2)l(-\sqrt3/2,1/2)\). A force along that derivative supplies positive virtual work, giving \[F_{min}=\frac{3(N-1)N^2}{4(3N-2)}Mg,\qquad\theta_F=5\pi/6.\] The force is 150 degrees from positive x, rather than necessarily perpendicular to the line from the fixed vertex.
